2. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the records.
3.

The Petitioners are apprehending arrest for the alleged commission of offence under Sections 109,115(2),126 (2),296,3(5) & 351(2) of BNS 2023 in G.R.Case No.809 of 2024 of the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal, arising out of Jarpada P.S.Case No.206 of 2024.
4. It is stated by the learned counsel for the petitioners that scuffle broke out between the two groups of the village with regard to a policy decision for payment of land acquisition compensation.
As a result of which both of sides sustained injuries.

He further contended that although some of the petitioners are having criminal antecedents i.e., the Petitioner No.1 is having two criminal antecedents, Petitioner No.3 having one criminal antecedent, petitioner No.4 is having three criminal antecedents, Petitioner No.5 is having one criminal antecedent and Petitioner No.8 is ) Subrat Das vs State Of Odisha .....

1 having two criminal antecedents, however they are ready and willing to abide by any stringent terms and conditions imposed by this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand objected to the release of the petitioner on bail on the ground that injuries sustained by the injured are grievous in nature.
It was submitted that the injured has sustained fracture injuries.
Furthermore, it was also submitted that although there are other laceration injuries, these are simple in nature.
He further submitted that in the event the petitioners are released on pre-arrest bail, there is a likelihood that they might indulge in similar offences.

6. Learned counsel for the State submitted that the investigation is still on therefore release of the petitioners at this stage might delay conclusion of the investigation and subsequent filing of the charge sheet.

7. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the both sides, and the case diary and the materials on record this Court is of the observation that two groups have indulged in a free fight pertaining to some dispute in the village.
As a result of such fight, some persons have sustained injuries.
Although, some of the injuries sustained are grievous in nature, a specific allegation of overt act has been made against petitioner Nos.2, 4, 5 and 7.
Considering the facts of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioners.

8. However, on the submission of the learned counsel, the Petitioner Nos.2, 4, 5 and 7 are given liberty to surrender before the learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal in the aforesaid case in the first hour within 21 working days hence and move for bail.
On such event, the learned Magistrate shall consider their application for bail in the first hour strictly on the basis of the materials on record.
In case of rejection of the bail application, the Petitioner Nos.2, 4, 5 and 7 may move for bail before the higher forum in the second hour.

On such event, the higher forum shall consider and dispose of the bail application of the Petitioner Nos.2, 4, 5 and 7 on the same day strictly on the basis of the materials on record, by maintaining the principles of parity, if applicable.
9. Case Diary be made available to the concerned courts.
Records be transmitted to the higher forum at the cost of the Petitioner Nos.2, 4, 5 and 7, if applied for.
10. So far as the rest of petitioners i.e. Petitioner Nos.1, 3, 6 and 8 are concerned

, it is observed that,
in the event the Petitioner Nos.1, 3, 6 and 8 surrender and move for bail within a period of four weeks from today, they shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
11. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
12. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
